fact_en: Cockroaches, grasshoppers, dragonflies, and crickets all go through incomplete metamorphosis — just three stages!
fact_bis: Ang mga uk-ok, apan, tabanog, ug gangis moagi sa dili kompleto nga metamorphosis nga adunay tulo ra ka hugna!

findings.note: EN lists "cockroaches, grasshoppers, dragonflies, and crickets"; the Cebuano renders dragonfly as `tabanog`, which is a KITE (the flying toy), not an insect. Never corrected in the card, so the incomplete-metamorphosis list contains a toy. Corpus check confirms the error is isolated: the 7 other cards containing `tabanog` are all about kites, while dragonfly is rendered `tutubi`/`alindanaw`/`alindahaw` in 23 other cards.

fact_en: A new queen ant digs a small chamber and raises her very first babies all by herself — once they grow into workers, they take over finding food so she can just lay eggs!
fact_bis: Ang bag-o nga reyna sa langgam mokalot og gamayng lungag ug mag-inusara nga mag-atiman sa iyang unang mga anak — kung modako na sila isip trabahante, sila na ang mangita og pagkaon para sa reyna!

findings.note: Queen-ant card: the body opens "Ang bag-o nga reyna sa langgam mokalot og gamayng lungag" — `langgam` is BIRD in Cebuano (ant = `hulmigas`/`hantik`; `langgam`=ant is Tagalog interference). The body never says ant again, so a child reads that a new queen BIRD digs a chamber and raises workers. Only the compact title_bis ("Reyna sa Hulmigas") is correct. Same false-friend appears elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. ffct-00110, an ants card titled "Langgam sa Matag Tawo"), so the grep is worth running.

fact_en: The Sulu bleeding-heart dove is one of the rarest birds in the Philippines, found only on the islands of Sulu and Tawi-Tawi!
fact_bis: Ang Sulu bleeding-heart dove usa sa pinakalangitnon nga langgam sa Pilipinas, makita lamang sa mga pulo sa Sulu ug Tawi-Tawi!

findings.note: EN: "one of the rarest birds in the Philippines". Cebuano: "usa sa pinakalangitnon nga langgam" — `langitnon` means heavenly/celestial, not rare (`talagsaon`). The card's headline fact (rarity) is gone and replaced with a meaningless claim; "makita lamang sa Sulu ug Tawi-Tawi" gives restricted range, not rarity, so it is not recoverable. `langitnon` occurs nowhere else in the corpus, so this is a one-off, not a convention.

fact_en:
What jobs do worker ants do?

Worker ants are female ants that cannot have babies — instead they search for food, guard the nest, and take care of the eggs and larvae.
fact_bis:
Unsay trabaho sa manggagawang langgam?

Ang manggagawang langgam mga babaye nga langgam nga dili na makapanamkon — hinuon, nangita sila og pagkaon, nagbantay sa pugad, ug nag-atiman sa mga itlog ug larva.

findings.note: Worker ants become birds. EN "Worker ants are female ants that cannot have babies" -> BIS "Unsay trabaho sa manggagawang langgam? Ang manggagawang langgam mga babaye nga langgam nga dili na makapanamkon... nagbantay sa pugad". In Cebuano langgam = BIRD (Tagalog false friend; other cards in this same batch use langgam correctly for birds, e.g. ffct-04634 "Philippine bulbul usa ka lumad nga langgam"). Reinforced by "pugad" (bird nest) instead of salag/balay sa hulmigas. The body never says ant; only title_bis ("Mamumuo nga Hulmigas") disagrees, so the answer text a child reads teaches that worker BIRDS are sterile females that tend eggs and larvae.

fact_en:
Can a fungus control an ant's mind?

The Ophiocordyceps fungus infects carpenter ants and takes control of their behavior — forcing the ant to climb to a certain height on a plant before it dies, then releasing spores from its head.
fact_bis:
Makakontrol ba sa hunahuna sa langgam ang fungus?

Ang Ophiocordyceps nga fungus mosulod sa lawas sa carpenter ant ug mokontrol sa iyang gawi — mopugos sa langgam nga mokatkat sa piho nga gitas-on sa tanom sa dili pa mamatay, dayon molabas og mga spore gikan sa ulo niini.

findings.note: Zombie-fungus card asks about the wrong animal. EN "Can a fungus control an ant's mind? ...infects carpenter ants... forcing the ant to climb" -> BIS question "Makakontrol ba sa hunahuna sa LANGGAM ang fungus?" and "mopugos sa LANGGAM nga mokatkat". langgam = bird in Cebuano, so the question and the key clause are about a bird; the only ant reference left is the untranslated English "carpenter ant", which a grade-5 Cebuano reader cannot be expected to decode. Child comes away believing Ophiocordyceps mind-controls birds.

fact_en: The patola (loofah) is a climbing vine vegetable that's cooked while young, and when left to ripen, its dried fibers become a natural scrubbing sponge.
fact_bis: Ang patola usa ka nagakatay nga utanon nga ginaluto samtang bata pa, ug kon tugotan nga mohinog, ang gahi nga himbis niini mahimong natural nga panghugas.

findings.note: Patola/loofah card: EN "when left to ripen, its dried fibers become a natural scrubbing sponge" -> BIS "ang gahi nga himbis niini mahimong natural nga panghugas". himbis = SCALES (fish/reptile/pangolin scales — that is how the corpus uses it elsewhere, e.g. ffct-04748 pangolin). Fiber is lanot/himaymay in this same corpus (ffct-00202 "Lanot sa Pinya", ffct-04806 "himaymay"). Nothing in the card corrects it, so the child is told the loofah sponge comes from hard scales/rind rather than dried fibers.

fact_en: It's better to blow your nose gently — blowing too hard can actually hurt your ears.
fact_bis: Mas maayo nga hinay-hinay huypon ang ilong — kay ang sobra ka kusog nga paghuyop mahimong makasakit sa dalunggan.

findings.note: title_bis "Hinay nga Pagsinghot" for "Blow Nose Gently" — singhot is sniffing/inhaling through the nose, the opposite direction from blowing out; the body correctly says "hinay-hinay huypon ang ilong". Flagged because it is the title (headline read on its own) and it reverses the direction of the very action the card is teaching, not just wording.

fact_en:
Why do baby warty pigs have stripes?

They're born with stripes on their bodies — a clever pattern that helps them hide from danger!
fact_bis:
Nganong adunay badlis ang anak sa baboy ihalas?

Natawo sila nga adunay badlis sa lawas — usa ka maalamon nga dibuho nga makatabang nila motago gikan sa peligro!

findings.note: title_bis "Uyok sa Baboy Ramo" for "Warty Pig Piglets". uyok is not the young of an animal (it is marrow/pith; the only other corpus uses are ffct-24119 and ffct-33414 where it is stretched to mean faint/weak). The body correctly says "anak sa baboy ihalas", so the title is the defect: it does not name piglets at all. Lower severity than the other three — flagged only because title_bis was called out for checking.

fact_en:
How long can giant clams live?

Giant clams can live a very long time — some reach more than 100 years old!
fact_bis:
Unsa kadugay mabuhi ang taklobo?

Ang taklobo makabuhi ug dugay kaayo — adunay moabot pa gani ug kapin sa 100 ka tuig!

findings.note: The card's fact is that pollen triggers a SNEEZE via histamine, but the Cebuano says `magsipon ka sa polen` / `mao nga magsipon ka` - sipon is colds/runny nose, never sneeze (the corpus uses bahing for sneeze and sip-on specifically for virus-caused colds, e.g. ffct-12167 'daghang lainlaing virus ang hinungdan sa sip-on', ffct-13177 'Makatakod ang sip-on kay virus ang hinungdan'). Neither the title (`Histamine sa Polen`) nor the body restores the sneeze, so a child reads that pollen gives you colds - contradicting the corpus's own virus cards. Lower confidence than the first flag, since a runny nose is also a real pollen symptom.

fact_en: A moth's feelers, or antennae, are often bushy and feathery.
fact_bis: Ang mga sungot o antena sa kabkab kasagaran daghan ug morag balhibo.

findings.note: Moth card: body says "antena sa kabkab", title_bis says "Anunghoy". Neither names a moth recognisably — 'kabkab' is the cassava cracker (see ffct-18262) and this same corpus also uses it for TOAD (ffct-06098, ffct-10639, ffct-05158); 'anunghoy' occurs exactly once in 47k cards, i.e. not a word. Corpus standard for moth is anunugba / gamu-gamo (33+ cards). Child reading only the Cebuano cannot tell which animal has feathery antennae.

fact_en:
What's the difference between frogs and toads?

Frogs have smooth, moist skin and need water to live, while toads have dry, bumpy skin and live on land.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang kalainan sa baki ug bakulaw?

Ang baki adunay hapsay, basa nga panit ug nanginahanglan og tubig aron mabuhi, samtang ang bakulaw adunay uga, bukol-bukol nga panit ug nagpuyo sa yuta.

findings.note: Frogs-vs-toads card renders 'toad' as 'bakulaw', which in Bisaya means a large ape / monster, not an amphibian. The card only lists traits (dry bumpy skin, lives on land) and never identifies bakulaw as a toad-type animal, so the frog/toad contrast is not learnable. Flagged with moderate confidence — note the corpus is unstable on 'toad' (bakulaw, kabkab, kabakaba, plain 'toad' all appear), so a Cebuano reviewer should pick one standard term.

fact_en:
Does the echidna have venom too?

The echidna, a relative of the platypus, also has a leg spur — but it doesn't release venom.
fact_bis:
Aduna ba pud hilo ang echidna?

Ang echidna, paryente sa platypus, adunay tibo pud sa tiil — apan dili kini mogula og hilo.

findings.note: title_bis "Echidna nga Tuko Walay Hilo" for EN "Echidna's Harmless Spur": 'tuko' is the gecko (corpus ffct-01153 "Tuko sa Balay"), so the standalone title labels the echidna a gecko. Body does restore it ("paryente sa platypus… adunay tibo pud sa tiil"), so this is title-only — same class as the cat-card-titled-iro defect. Likely a mangling of 'tunok' (spine); weakest of the four.
